title: Signed totalization of the perfect formula
statement:
For a bounded finite-projective complex $F^\bullet$, the total arrows
$\pi_{h,E,F}$ and $\rho_{h,E,F}$ are inverse isomorphisms.

proof.text: Use the ringed-topos morphism $h:(\mathcal T,S)\to(\mathcal S,R)$, $E\in D(S)$, and the bounded strict-perfect package on $F$ of [def-weil-pbc-projection-formula-arrows]. All sites are small in the chosen universe. Choose a K-injective representative $I$ of $E$ by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist], and put $A=h_*I$. Use the shifts and cone triangles of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Applying an additive functor to a shifted complex or to a cone applies it to each entry of the differential matrix; hence $Qh_*$ is exact on homotopy categories. By [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived], its comparison $QA\to Rh_*E$ is an isomorphism. Throughout, use these canonical comparisons rather than arbitrary isomorphisms between representatives.

source.place: First sentence: choose a representative of Rh_*E; foundations: Stacks 079P and 070K

proof.text: For every $r$ the package gives $p_ri_r=1$ on $F^r$. Tensoring with $F^r$ is therefore a retract of tensoring with $R^{N_r}$, a finite power of the identity. On any short exact sequence its tensor sequence is a direct summand of a finite power of that exact sequence, so is exact. Thus $F^r$ is flat. Pulling back the splitting gives the same assertion for $h^*F^r$ over $S$, since $h^*R^{N_r}=S^{N_r}$. Boundedness and [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site] make $F$ K-flat; [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] makes $h^*F$ K-flat with flat terms and identifies it with $Lh^*F$. No exactness of $h^*$ on arbitrary modules is assumed.

source.place: First sentence: validity of the strict-perfect tensor model; Stacks 06YQ and 0G7E

proof.text: Put $C=\operatorname{Tot}(A\otimes_R F)$ and $J=\operatorname{Tot}(I\otimes_S h^*F)$. Choose a K-flat resolution with flat terms $v:P\to A$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. The criterion [lem-pur-quasi-iso-cone-acyclic] makes $\operatorname{Cone}(v)$ acyclic. Its tensor with $F$ is acyclic by [def-pc-kflat-complex]. This tensor is the cone of $v\otimes1$: write $\operatorname{Cone}(v)^a=A^a\oplus P^{a+1}$ as in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. On the $P^{a+1}\otimes F^r$ summand the second differential has sign $(-1)^a$; in the cone of $v\otimes1$ its sign is $-(-1)^{a+1}=(-1)^a$, and the other matrix entries agree. Thus the criterion proves that $P\otimes F\to C$ is a quasi-isomorphism. The canonical two-K-flat comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] therefore identifies $QC$ with $Rh_*E\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}F$. Resolving $I$ in the same way and tensoring with $h^*F$ gives $QJ=E\otimes_S^{\mathbf L}Lh^*F$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-split-perfect-tensor-kinjective] to $I$ and the pulled-back splitting of $F$: $J$ is K-injective. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived] identifies $Q(h_*J)$ with $Rh_*(E\otimes_S^{\mathbf L}Lh^*F)$. Write $B=h_*J$. The cone argument uses only the defining test against acyclic complexes, not a claim that $A$ or $I$ is K-flat.

source.place: First sentence and displayed total complexes; Stacks 06YS, 06YU, 0A96, 070K, and 05RT (cone criterion)

proof.text: For an $S$-module $M$ and an $R$-module $H$ let $t_{M,H}:h_*M\otimes_R H\to h_*(M\otimes_S h^*H)$ be the ordinary adjunct of $\varepsilon_M\otimes1$ after the natural pullback-tensor isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-pullback-tensor]. The counit and adjunction are natural by [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy]. For $H=R^N$, the composites of $t_{M,R^N}$ with the $N$ projections are the identity adjuncts on $h_*M$. Therefore this is the finite-product comparison, which is invertible by [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-limits]. Write $q_{M,N}$ for its inverse. Also $B^n=h_*(\bigoplus_{a+r=n}I^a\otimes h^*F^r)$ is the finite sum of the termwise pushforwards: $r$ lies in a fixed finite interval, and finite sums equal finite products. This holds even when $I$ is unbounded, and includes the empty sum.

source.place: Term maps before totalization; Stacks 03EL and 0038

proof.text:
Set $t_{a,r}=t_{I^a,F^r}$ and $s_{a,r}=(1\otimes p_r)q_{I^a,N_r}h_*(1\otimes h^*i_r)$, the formula specified in [def-weil-pbc-projection-formula-arrows]. Naturality gives $h_*(1\otimes h^*i_r)t_{a,r}=t_{I^a,R^{N_r}}(1\otimes i_r)$ and $h_*(1\otimes h^*p_r)t_{I^a,R^{N_r}}=t_{a,r}(1\otimes p_r)$. Substituting these two equations and $p_ri_r=1$ gives
$$s_{a,r}t_{a,r}=(1\otimes p_r)q_{I^a,N_r}t_{I^a,R^{N_r}}(1\otimes i_r)=1,$$
$$t_{a,r}s_{a,r}=h_*(1\otimes h^*p_r)t_{I^a,R^{N_r}}q_{I^a,N_r}h_*(1\otimes h^*i_r)=1.$$
These equations hold for actual module-sheaf maps, before passing to the derived category.

source.place: Second paragraph: the summand inverse equations, expanded at chain level

proof.text: For a map $u:F^r\to F^{r+1}$, write $A(u)=1\otimes u$ and $B(u)=h_*(1\otimes h^*u)$. Counit naturality gives $B(u)t_r=t_{r+1}A(u)$. Multiplication on the left by $s_{r+1}$ and on the right by $s_r$ gives $s_{r+1}B(u)=A(u)s_r$. For a map $w:I^a\to I^{a+1}$ the same naturality is $h_*(w\otimes1)t_{a,r}=t_{a+1,r}(h_*w\otimes1)$, and multiplication by the two inverses gives $s_{a+1,r}h_*(w\otimes1)=(h_*w\otimes1)s_{a,r}$. Apply these formulas to $u=d_F$ and $w=d_I$. Thus both families commute with both differentials. The splitting maps $i_r,p_r$ need not commute with $d_F$: naturality of their resulting inverse follows from the inverse equations, not from any compatibility of the chosen presentations.

source.place: Second paragraph: naturality and uniqueness of inverses, applied to both differentials

proof.text: On bidegree $(a,r)$, [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] gives differential $d_I\otimes1+(-1)^a1\otimes d_F$. The two families preserve both indices. Hence the square for the first differential has coefficient $1$ on each side, and the square for the second has the same coefficient $(-1)^a$ on each side. Adding the squares gives $dt=td$ and $ds=sd$. Extend over the finite sum in each degree, using Step 4 for $B$. The restrictions of $st$ and $ts$ to every summand are identities by Step 5, so the universal property of the direct sum gives $st=1_C$ and $ts=1_B$ as chain maps. This is the signed totalization argument, including all Koszul signs.

source.place: Displayed differential and final paragraph: inverse total chain maps

proof.text: The complex $P\otimes F$ of Step 3 is K-flat with flat terms. Indeed for any acyclic $Z$, the ordinary tensor associator identifies $Z\otimes(P\otimes F)$ with $(Z\otimes P)\otimes F$. On indices $(a,b,r)$ the three differential coefficients are $1,(-1)^a,(-1)^{a+b}$ on both sides. The latter complex is acyclic, first by K-flatness of $P$ and then by K-flatness of $F$, directly from [def-pc-kflat-complex]. In each total degree only finitely many $r$ occur; each $P^a\otimes F^r$ is a retract of $(P^a)^{N_r}$. Tensoring a short exact sequence with the resulting finite sum is therefore a direct summand of finite sums of exact sequences, proving flatness of its terms. This is a direct three-line associativity/acyclicity argument, as in Stacks 07A2 (lemma-tensor-product-K-flat), with the signs and the flat-term condition written out.

source.place: First sentence: a resolving representative for the source of the derived adjunct; Stacks 07A2

proof.text: Consequently $v\otimes1:P\otimes F\to C$ is a valid K-flat resolution with flat terms. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback], applying $h^*$ computes $Lh^*(QC)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], the canonical comparison $Lh^*(QA\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}F)\to Lh^*QA\otimes_S^{\mathbf L}Lh^*F$ is represented on this resolution by $h^*(P\otimes F)\cong h^*P\otimes h^*F$. Here the ordinary isomorphism is the termwise map of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-pullback-tensor]. It extends over the finite sums because an additive functor preserves biproducts: the images of the injections and projections satisfy the same finite identity $\sum\iota_r\mathrm{pr}_r=1$. Thus this is the specified canonical comparison, with the same tensor differential, rather than an unspecified isomorphism.

source.place: First sentence: canonical derived pullback-tensor comparison; Stacks 06YY, 07A4, 03EL

proof.text:
Apply the representative formula of [lem-pc-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general] with target $K=J$, its right resolution the identity $J\to J$, source complex $M=C$, left resolution $v\otimes1:P\otimes F\to C$, and chain map $f=t\circ(v\otimes1):P\otimes F\to h_*J$. The right-resolution comparison is invertible because $J$ is K-injective (Step 3); the left one is invertible by Steps 8 and 9. That formula says the derived adjunct of $Qt:QC\to Rh_*(QJ)$ is represented, after its source comparison, by the ordinary adjunct of $f$. By the termwise adjunction of [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy] and the definition of $t$, this ordinary adjunct is
$$h^*P\otimes h^*F\xrightarrow{h^*v\otimes1}h^*h_*I\otimes h^*F\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_I\otimes1}I\otimes h^*F.$$
The equation holds on every bidegree by definition of $t_{a,r}$ and hence on the finite total complex.

source.place: Identification of the total arrow with its defining adjunct; Stacks 0DVC/0FND representative formula

proof.text: Use the same representative formula of [lem-pc-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general] with $K=I$, $M=A$, right resolution the identity, left resolution $v:P\to A$, and $f=v:P\to h_*I=A$. The represented derived arrow is the identity of $Rh_*E$: the factor $Qv$ cancels the inverted source resolution. Its adjunct is the derived counit $\varepsilon_E$. Thus $h^*P\xrightarrow{h^*v}h^*h_*I\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_I}I$, with its source comparison, represents precisely $\varepsilon_E$. Tensoring this representative with the K-flat complex $h^*F$ represents $\varepsilon_E\otimes1$: tensoring with that factor preserves quasi-isomorphisms by the cone argument of Step 3, so the same statement holds after inverting the source comparison. The natural two-K-flat tensor comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] fixes these identifications. Combining with Step 9, the adjunct computed in Step 10 is exactly the adjunct defining $\pi_{h,E,F}$ in [def-weil-pbc-projection-formula-arrows]. Injectivity of the adjunction bijection gives $Qt=\pi_{h,E,F}$.

source.place: Identification with the canonical projection arrow, using its counit definition; Stacks 0DVC/0FND and 06YU

proof.text: The chain map $s$ is exactly the map used to define $\rho_{h,E,F}$ in [def-weil-pbc-projection-formula-arrows]: Step 5 used its displayed $q,i_r,p_r$ formula on each bidegree, Step 4 its finite-sum identification, and Steps 6 and 7 its differential convention. Hence $Qs=\rho_{h,E,F}$. For a single coefficient term this agrees with the derived summand inverse of [lemma-weil-pbc-projection-formula-projective-summand]; no choice of a new inverse is being made. Apply localization to the actual chain equations in Step 7. Since it preserves identities and composition, they become $\rho_{h,E,F}\pi_{h,E,F}=1$ and $\pi_{h,E,F}\rho_{h,E,F}=1$. Thus the specified total arrows are inverse isomorphisms.

proof_origin.place: Both proof paragraphs, expanded using the canonical ringed-topos adjunction and Stacks 079P, 070K, 06YS, 0A96, 03EL, 07A4, 0DVC/0FND.
